summary: American chess prodigy Bobby Fischer won the 1972 world title as a Cold War hero, then spent decades spreading antisemitic conspiracy theories and played a 1992 sanctions-busting match that served Milosevic's regime during the Bosnian genocide.

evidence.note: Fischer's 1943 birth in Chicago to a homeless single mother
US junior title and the 1956 Game of the Century at age thirteen
1958 Soviet visit ends in scandal; Tito's Yugoslavia hosts him instead
early antisemitic statements, including the 1962 Harper's interview
1972 Iceland match, Kissinger calls, Cold War symbolism
buys the Protocols and Klassen's book; turns to Nazi propaganda
long segment on the Bosnian genocide around the 1992 match
Vasiljevic's bank as a Ponzi scheme used to evade sanctions
9/11 radio interview calling for persecution of Jews
2004 arrest and detention in Japan, then Icelandic citizenship
death in an Icelandic hospital; later exhumation over the estate

notes: Mia Wong presents and Robert Evans is the guest. Primary theme is sports per the taxonomy example; nazism chosen alongside racism because Fischer distributed Nazi pamphlets and denied the Holocaust. The Sveti Stefan opening games put ME in play, but it was dropped for the six-country limit. The Najdorf opening segment is background, not counted in the spans. The 2010 exhumation is a brief coda, so it is not counted.
